overview: The features package is the middle of the volforecast pipeline: it turns cleaned daily measures (realized variance, realized quarticity, semivariances from the data layer) plus enriched market columns (the IV surface, VIX futures, credit spreads merged upstream by IVSurfaceLayer) into the design matrix consumed by the HAR OLS baselines and LightGBM models. It is organized as layers 0-6, each a class registered into FEATURE_REGISTRY via the register_feature_layer decorator with a uniform compute(daily_data, context) -> DataFrame contract, so a config can list which layers to stack. Layer 0 (har_core) is the HAR backbone: log RV at daily, weekly (5 day) and monthly (22 day) horizons plus HARQ realized-quarticity terms. Layer 1 (asymmetry) adds leverage-effect signals: positive and negative semivariances, bipower variation, jump variation. Layer 2 (options) derives forward-looking signals from the SPX IV surface: variance risk premium, 25-delta skew, term slope, 0DTE and 1W tenors, VVIX, VIX futures term structure, and IV x log RV interactions. Layer 3 (microstructure) covers order flow: VPIN, Kyle's lambda, Amihud illiquidity from 10 second bars. Layer 4 (cross_asset) plus cross_asset_momentum bring rate, FX, credit, and commodity volatility, and calendar (Layer 5) encodes FOMC, NFP, and OpEx proximity that is known in advance. Further registered layers extend the stack: dealer_gamma (SPX gamma exposure), implied_correlation and realized_correlation, gsvivs_signals (the 73-feature set of the GSVIVS01 short-variance strategy), long_memory (60 and 90 day lags for h=22), regime (Markov-switching probabilities), vol_of_vol, and noise_robust. Naming is systematic: _d is the daily value, _w a 5 day rolling mean, _m a 22 day rolling mean; momentum features use d_*_1d, d_*_5d, and z_* rolling z-scores. One quirk: the package docstring says layers 0-6, but only Layers 0-5 are named in file docstrings; no file is explicitly labelled Layer 6.

modules.role: Eighteen feature-layer modules that convert daily realized measures and enriched market data into model-ready columns for vol forecasting. Each layer is a class decorated with register_feature_layer(name) from volforecast.registry, exposing compute(daily_data, context) and returning a DataFrame aligned to daily_data.index, so layers compose declaratively from config. Numbered layers 0-5 live in har.py, asymmetry.py, options.py, microstructure.py, cross_asset.py, and calendar.py; the remaining modules (dealer_gamma, gsvivs_signals, implied_correlation, realized_correlation, cross_asset_momentum, long_memory, regime, vol_of_vol, noise_robust) are registered extensions without an explicit layer number. Shared helpers live in transforms.py (safe_log with a 1e-20 floor, lagged_log_features producing the _d/_w/_m suffix families) and expansion.py (triple_expand into level/change/zscore for LightGBM only). Inputs come from volforecast.data (measures, micro, gex_ingest, options_oi caches under data/raw/); outputs feed the HAR OLS and LightGBM model stages downstream. Several layers degrade gracefully to empty or all-NaN frames when their cache or columns are missing, which matters on this restored snapshot where data/raw caches may be absent.

glossary.definition: Heterogeneous autoregressive model: forecasts volatility from realized variance averaged at daily, weekly (5d), and monthly (22d) horizons.
A fourth-moment measure of intraday returns used as a measurement-quality proxy; HARQ interacts it with RV so the model trusts noisy RV less.
Option-implied variance minus realized variance, here (atm_iv/100)^2 - rv*252; usually positive because investors pay a premium for vol protection.
Implied volatility of options expiring the same day; an exact tenor match for one-day-ahead RV forecasting.
CBOE index of the implied volatility of VIX options: the market's vol-of-vol gauge, used here in levels, innovations, and a risk-premium spread.
Aggregate gamma of SPX option dealers; its sign and regime shape how dealer hedging dampens or amplifies realized volatility.
A jump-robust estimator of the continuous part of daily variance built from products of adjacent absolute returns.
Realized variance split into components from positive and negative intraday returns, capturing the leverage effect asymmetry.
Volume-synchronized probability of informed trading, a daily order-flow toxicity measure loaded from the microstructure cache.
Price impact coefficient: the OLS slope of price changes on signed order flow; higher values mean less liquidity or more informed trading.
Total connectedness of a multi-asset RV panel from a rolling VAR forecast error variance decomposition; high values flag systemic vol transmission.
Two-Scales Realized Volatility: combines all-tick and subsampled return grids to cancel microstructure noise bias in the variance estimate.
